Chocolate Avocado Mousse
Total: 1 hr 5 min
Active: 5 min
Yield: 2 servings
Level: Easy

Ingredients

1 large ripe avocado, cut into chunks
1/4 cup natural cocoa powder
1/4 cup unsweetened almond milk
1/4 cup maple syrup or agave
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
Pinch of sea salt
Suggested toppings: chia seeds, cocoa nibs, shredded coconut, chopped mango, chopped pineapple and pomegranate seeds 
Coconut Whipped Cream, recipe follows, for garnish, optional
Coconut Whipped Cream:
1 can coconut milk, refrigerated overnight until well chilled
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
Confectioners' sugar or sweetener of choice, to taste

Directions

In a blender, combine the avocado, cocoa powder, almond milk, maple syrup, vanilla and salt. Blend on medium until completely smooth, scraping down the sides of the blender often. Increase the speed to high and blend about 30 seconds to lighten the mousse. 

Spoon into 2 serving glasses or cups. If you have the time, chill in the refrigerator until cold, about an hour. If not, enjoy right away with the toppings of your choice and garnish with Coconut Whipped Cream if desired.

Coconut Whipped Cream:
Remove the can of coconut milk from the refrigerator without shaking it. Open the can, scrape out the solidified coconut cream from the top and put it in a mixing bowl. (Save the liquid in the bottom of the can for a smoothie.) Whip the coconut cream with an electric mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on high until light and fluffy, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the vanilla and confectioners' sugar or other sweetener to taste. Whip again and serve.

transcript.text:
Today on "Feel Good"
with me, Hannah,

we're making a chocolate mousse
with a secret ingredient.
Avocado.
[music playing]

I love this recipe because
it's the same consistency

as a regular mousse, but
it's totally guilt free.

The key to this is
using a ripe avocado.

The difference between
an unripe avocado

is that it's green
and hard to touch.

But a ripe avocado is brown
and very easy on the thumb.

So I love this recipe because
it's great for a dinner party

because you can make it
beforehand and chill it.

The reason why you want
to use a ripe avocado

is so that it all
blends very easily.

After I add the avocado, I'm
going to add the cocoa powder.

And cocoa powder is
full of antioxidants.

I'm also going to add an
unsweetened almond milk,

which makes this a really
great vegan dessert option.

But if dairy's
not an issue, then
you can use any milk you want.
Maple syrup as my sweetener.

But you can use honey
or agave instead.

But it should
definitely be liquid.

I'm also going to add vanilla
and a pinch of salt. Now

I'm going to blend this on
low for about two minutes.
[clock ticking]
[bell ding]
This looks about perfect.
Oh yeah.
It's light and creamy.
Exactly how we want it.
I've made two servings here.

And although you can
consume this immediately

and it is delicious, I think
it's much better after you
chill it for about 30 minutes.
Whoa.
Whoops.

While this is
chilling, I'm going

to clean up and get ready
for the best part-- toppings.
Now comes the fun part.

Here are all the toppings that
I'm going to use, at least.

But you can use whatever
toppings you'd like.
I'm doing a bunch of fruit.

I've got raspberries,
strawberries, and blueberries,

which I think adds like
a nice layer of sweetness
as well as color.

This is a great dessert
to make for a dinner party

because you could
have a little toppings

bar where everyone
puts their own toppings
on it which would be so cute.

Then I've made coconut
whipped cream, which

I think is great, super
easy, as an alternative
to regular whipped cream.

All you do is you take
a can of coconut milk

and you put it in
the refrigerator

overnight so that it
hardens and separates.

The top layer will
be hard like this

and underneath will be coconut
water, which you can use
for a smoothie or on its own.

Then I'm going to
add some cocoa nibs

which give it a
nice, crunchy layer,
as well as some chia seeds.
And even some coconut chips.
Let's taste this.
Mmm.
This is amazing.

I hope you enjoyed
the episode this week.

Catch me next time on "Feel
Good" with me, Hannah.

nodes.plm_caption:
A young woman is showing an ingredients and how to make a chocolate mousse. This is a food network television show segment. 

The woman is standing in front of a modern, kitchen island. She is wearing an old grey T-shirt and black pants. There is a cutting board and a blender sitting on the island. 

The woman first shows a variety of avocado products and then shows how to prepare chocolate mousse. She first puts 1/4 of an avocado, 1/3 cup of chocolate syrup in the blender. 

She then blends the ingredients together and puts them into two stemless wine glasses. She adds 1 scoop of coconut ice cream, 2 sliced blackberries, and 2 chopped strawberry halves. She then tops it off with chocolate chips.

summary.brief: Hannah prepares a silky avocado chocolate mousse, tops it with fresh fruit and crunchy toppings, and finishes with a recipe slide.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with Hannah introducing the "Feel Good" series and showing a ripe avocado. She explains how a ripe avocado feels softer than an unripe one, then scoops the flesh into a blender together with cocoa powder, unsweetened almond milk, maple syrup, vanilla extract and a pinch of sea salt. She blends on low for about two minutes until the mixture is smooth, light and creamy, and pours the mousse into two glasses. While the mousse chills, she describes how to make coconut whipped cream by chilling a can of coconut milk, scraping out the solid cream and whipping it with vanilla and sugar. She then decorates each glass with raspberries, strawberries, blueberries, cocoa nibs, chia seeds and coconut chips, noting the whipped coconut cream can be added as an alternative topping. Hannah tastes a spoonful, declares the mousse amazing, and ends the episode with a slide that displays the chocolate avocado mousse recipe and ingredient list.

action.detailed: Blend avocado, cocoa powder, almond milk, maple syrup, vanilla and salt in a blender until smooth, pour the mousse into two glasses, let it chill, optionally whip chilled coconut cream, and garnish each glass with berries, cocoa nibs, chia seeds and coconut chips before serving.
action.actor: Hannah Bronfman, the Food Network host

In the background is a kitchen with stainless steel counters and gray cupboards with lots of different kitchen items on the shelves. The overall mood of the video seems to be light-hearted as it is a cooking show and she seems very excited to be making the dessert.
The video starts with a woman placing something into the fridge. She pulls out two glass cups and two blue bowls with a white circle in the middle of them. She places the two cups on a board in front of her. She says, "In a few minutes." She takes the contents of the blue bowl in front of her and places it in the cup in front of her. "Now, add some fruit. What you want to top it with." She uses a spoon to put different fruits into the chocolate. "Now, go ahead and take a little bit of whipped cream and put it on top." She uses a spoon to spoon the whipped cream into each glass. "You can make it look all over the place because it is a quick little finish. You can add a little bit more if you want." She goes back to the blue bowls to add some more fresh berries to the cups. "We're going to use the unopened tin in the fridge behind you. You can pull them out right here in front of you. You can put that one inside each glass and top it off with some coconut milk." The woman adds the tin. "Now, put some more whipped cream on top and serve it right away. Enjoy! I just found an unopened one in the fridge here on the back wall and you can find one by yourself. Let me know how it turns out."

summary.brief: The woman tops the chocolate mousse glasses with fresh berries, coconut‑whipped cream and a splash of coconut milk.
summary.detailed: She pulls the two prepared mousse glasses from the refrigerator and sets them on a board, then spoons raspberries, strawberries and blueberries from the blue bowls into each glass. She adds a dollop of coconut‑whipped cream, opens an unopened tin of coconut milk from the fridge and pours a little into each glass, and finishes with a second swirl of whipped cream before presenting the finished desserts. The scene takes place in a bright modern kitchen with stainless‑steel appliances, gray cabinets and the woman wearing a grey top and blue jeans.

action.detailed: Place the mousse glasses on the board, spoon fresh berries into each, add a dollop of coconut‑whipped cream, pour a splash of coconut milk from the tin, and finish with an extra swirl of whipped cream.
action.actor: The woman in the grey top standing at the kitchen counter

She scoops the thick brown mousse from the blender, lifts and rotates the blender clockwise to let the mousse flow into the right‑hand glass, then repeats the motion for the left glass. After both glasses are filled she puts the blender back on the countertop, grabs the two glasses by their rims with both hands, pushes them forward toward the camera while leaning slightly to the left, and smiles as she makes a brief comment about the chocolate. The segment ends with her standing in front of a partially visible cabinet, her long dark hair reaching mid‑chest.

summary.brief: The woman adds black and red berries from a blue bowl into a glass of brown mousse.
summary.detailed: In an extreme close‑up, the woman wearing a gray top and black pants leans over a blue bowl filled with black and red berries. Holding a metal spoon in her right hand, she taps a berry with her thumb and fingers, lifts the spoon, and briefly shakes the berry in her left hand before returning to the bowl. She taps the spoon against the rim of the bowl, scoops another berry and drops it into a clear glass that already contains a quarter‑filled brown mousse. She repeats this motion two more times, depositing additional berries into the glass. The camera then pans up to show the now‑empty blue bowl behind the glass and returns to her as she prepares to take another spoonful of berries.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: Hannah Bronfman Makes Healthy Avocado Chocolate Mousse | Food Network
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
Subscribe ► http://foodtv.com/YouTube
Get the recipe ► https://foodtv.com/369rWtr

Welcome to Food Network, where learning to cook is as simple as clicking play! Grab your apron and get ready to get cookin' with some of the best chefs around the world. We'll give you a behind-the-scenes look at our best shows, take you inside our favorite restaurant and be your resource in the kitchen to make sure every meal is a 10/10!

Chocolate Avocado Mousse
Total: 1 hr 5 min
Active: 5 min
Yield: 2 servings
Level: Easy

Ingredients

1 large ripe avocado, cut into chunks
1/4 cup natural cocoa powder
1/4 cup
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The segment opens with Hannah introducing the "Feel Good" series and showing a ripe avocado. She explains how a ripe avocado feels softer than an unripe one, then scoops the flesh into a blender together with cocoa powder, unsweetened almond milk, maple syrup, vanilla extract and a pinch of sea salt. She blends on low for about two minutes until the mixture is smooth, light and creamy, and pours the mousse into two glasses. While the mousse chills, she describes how to make coconut whipped cream by chilling a can of coconut milk, scraping out the solid cream and whipping it with vanilla and sugar. She then decorates each glass with raspberries, strawberries, blueberries, cocoa nibs, chia seeds and coconut chips, noting the whipped coconut cream can be added as an alternative topping. Hannah tastes a spoonful, declares the mousse amazing, and ends the episode with a slide that displays the chocolate avocado mousse recipe and ingredient list.
action_list: Taste mousse and rest hands on glasses
Add fruit and coconut whipped cream to dessert glasses
Top mousse with fruit and cream
Add almond milk and maple syrup to blender
Add berry and chia seed toppings
Add cocoa powder; display white powder
Add vanilla extract and sea salt to blender
Add fresh berries to dessert glasses
Add cocoa powder and pour mixture

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
